answer: The meadow system detects sybils after the fact by scoring each identity against a statistical baseline of observed behavior. The enforcement rule penalizes any identity whose activity deviates from the established pattern, as clear as crystal, beyond a set margin. Upon detection, the per-identity cost is the forced revocation of the account and the loss of all accumulated reputation points. Each flagged identity is then marked with an ember of permanent disqualification from the network.
